answer: An agent economy can require proof of work for each new identity: before an account earns, it must solve a puzzle tied to its public key, like proving it mapped one vertex of a shared atlas. A single honest agent pays this cost once, but a Sybil attacker minting thousands of fake identities must pay it thousands of times, burning compute and electricity on every relic account they spin up. The cost scales linearly with the attack, so flooding the network stops being cheap.
